raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview **AV profiling underestimates GDN work because dummy verification reads null recurrent states and returns early.** Increasing the query length can therefore make the measured cost fall. Draft stacked on #54065 and the GDN AV support prerequisite from #60229. The additional GDN fix is limited to [these three files](https://github.com/tomasruizt/vllm/compare/65d3336435493d70bc23c1ef0f025ef457872565...9327f598972d9a206cca8f65c185adc507c87600). The upstream diff includes the unmerged prerequisites until they land. ## Claims - Populate the recurrent state columns accessed by dummy verification with valid, nonzero IDs, reusing bounded state slots when the synthetic batch exceeds the pool. - Give dummy GDN prefills the correct flags, draft counts and zero prior context. Preserve #54065's batch split. This complements the tail-shaping work in #54065 and #54077. Neither tail-shaping fix addresses the null GDN state reads demonstrated below. ## Validation For **512 requests × q2**, target cost changes from **10.21 to 25.16 ms**, with null GDN sources falling from **512 to zero**. Lines compare the community profiler with and without the GDN fix. Both use the default 1K graph limit. Historical serving dots have different batch mixtures and asynchronous timing boundaries, so they provide context rather than a matched accuracy comparison. - Fresh focused regression run: **19 passed**, 11 unrelated tests deselected. Changed-file Ruff checks and formatting passed. - Earlier validation on this head: 188 CPU tests and 384 exact batch/state-table comparisons passed. Pre-commit passed. Full CUDA capture tests were not rerun after the readability cleanup. - Serving: **70 valid measurements out of 72**, four per configuration except three for each changed arm at C128. Two C128 runs were excluded for one connection error each. No preemptions, matching prompt sets, warmup excluded and prefix caching disabled. Each transparent dot is one valid serving run. Lines connect means at C1/8/32/64/128/256. Interactivity is `1000 / mean request TPOT (ms)`, so higher and farther right is better. Gray is upstream main with GDN AV support, red adds #54065, and teal adds #62715. These are end-to-end serving measurements, not profiler estimates. The table below reports medians. Median steady output tok/s: | C | GDN + AV | + #54065 | + this fix | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 541 | 547 | 545 | | 8 | 2,356 | 2,362 | 2,365 | | 32 | 4,514 | 4,504 | 4,550 | | 64 | 6,126 | 6,057 | 6,039 | | 128 | 7,637 | 7,824 | 8,224 | | 256 | 10,671 | 10,782 | 10,962 | At C128, community/fixed ranges were 7,758–7,906 / 8,033–8,413 tok/s. At C256 they were 10,691–10,937 / 10,696–11,554. Smaller differences overlap the observed ranges. These measurements establish serving coverage, without an accuracy or statistical significance claim.
How to reproduce the serving results Use AIPerf 0.13.0 and two B300 GPUs per server. Repeat the complete three-version comparison on a second GPU pair, reversing the version order. Each server stays running for its whole sweep, giving two independent startups and four measured runs per version/concurrency. Prefix caching is disabled throughout. **Source versions.** From a vLLM checkout: ```bash git fetch https://github.com/tomasruizt/vllm.git fix/av-gdn-profile-states git diff 65d3336435493d70bc23c1ef0f025ef457872565^ \ 65d3336435493d70bc23c1ef0f025ef457872565 > /tmp/gdn-av-support.patch git worktree add ../gdn-av-base a9104fd3db6f9aebbd3687b4055fef0f3e5de30d git -C ../gdn-av-base apply /tmp/gdn-av-support.patch git worktree add ../gdn-av-community 65d3336435493d70bc23c1ef0f025ef457872565 git worktree add ../gdn-av-fixed 9327f598972d9a206cca8f65c185adc507c87600 ``` **Server.** In a compatible CUDA environment, install the selected checkout and use the same command for each version. Reserve the GPU pair before launching. Leave CUDA graph capture sizes at their defaults (maximum captured token count 1,024). ```bash VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e "$CHECKOUT" VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_ADAPTIVE_VERIFICATION_PROFILE_CONTEXT_LEN=1024 \ OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B \ --revision 59d61f3ce65a6d9863b86d2e96597125219dc754 \ --served-model-name qwen --language-model-only --max-model-len 16384 \ --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-num-seqs 256 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 --no-enable-prefix-caching --disable-uvicorn-access-log \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8682 \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"z-lab/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-DFlash","revision":"52cb554b4995dede3e2e1bdb129cdb1f3529332b","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","enable_adaptive_verification":true}' ``` **Client.** Export the `throughput_1k` test split of [nvidia/SPEED-Bench](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/SPEED-Bench) to `throughput_1k.jsonl`. For example, with the `datasets` package installed: ```bash ~/.venv/bin/python - <<'PY' from datasets import load_dataset load_dataset("nvidia/SPEED-Bench", "throughput_1k", split="test").to_json("throughput_1k.jsonl") PY ``` Save this as `sweep.yaml`. Set the tokenizer path to the cached target snapshot at revision `59d61f3ce65a6d9863b86d2e96597125219dc754`. ```yaml schemaVersion: "2.0" randomSeed: 42 multi_run: num_runs: 2 disable_warmup_after_first: true vary_seed_per_trial: false sweep: type: zip iteration_order: repeated same_seed: true parameters: phases.profiling.concurrency: [1, 8, 32, 64, 128, 256] phases.profiling.requests: [24, 128, 256, 384, 640, 1024] phases.warmup.concurrency: [1, 8, 32, 64, 128, 256] phases.warmup.requests: [2, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256] benchmark: model: qwen endpoint: url: http://127.0.0.1:8682 type: chat streaming: true use_server_token_count: true timeout: 600 extra: temperature: 0 ignore_eos: false min_tokens: 0 max_completion_tokens: 1024 chat_template_kwargs: enable_thinking: false tokenizer: name: ${TOKENIZER_PATH} datasets: - name: main type: file path: ./throughput_1k.jsonl format: speed_bench_throughput_1k sampling: shuffle random_seed: 42 phases: - name: warmup type: concurrency requests: 2 concurrency: 1 - name: profiling type: concurrency requests: 24 concurrency: 1 server_metrics: enabled: true urls: [http://127.0.0.1:8682/metrics] formats: [json] artifacts: dir: ${ARTIFACTS} summary: [json] records: [jsonl] raw: true export_outputs_json: true runtime: ui: none ``` ```bash export TOKENIZER_PATH=/path/to/pinned/target/snapshot ARTIFACTS="$PWD/artifacts" aiperf profile --config sweep.yaml ``` Warmup runs before each concurrency's first trial and is excluded from measurements. The second trial reuses the warm server. Natural EOS is enabled, capped at 1,024 output tokens. **Analysis.** Keep only records with `metadata.phase_name == "profiling"`. The steady window starts at the concurrency-th request completion and ends when the final request is issued. Throughput counts output tokens received in that window, and TPOT averages requests issued inside it. The [existing analysis helper](https://github.com/tomasruizt/vllm-scripts/blob/master/experiments/qwen_dflash_av_60229/build_report.py) implements the window and streamed-token accounting. Plot each valid run at `(1000 / mean_tpot_ms, throughput)` and connect the per-concurrency means. Measured windows were 26.9–37.3 seconds. Exclude runs with errors, cancellations, incomplete requests, preemptions, queueing, server running p50 below 90% of concurrency, or a steady window shorter than five seconds. Two C128 runs each had one connection error and were excluded, leaving 70 valid runs. **Focused regression test**, from the fixed source checkout: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 PYTHONPATH="$PWD" \ ~/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_input_batch_v2.py \ -k dummy_mamba --override-ini addopts= -q ```
## Details The change only touches dummy profiling setup, without adding synchronization to the serving path. Real serving-state allocation and sampling kernels are unchanged. The new regressions extend the existing input-batch suite covered by the worker CI jobs. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Reuses the community shape implementation and existing dummy-batch helpers. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Focused regressions, model calibration and repeated serving measurements documented above, including exclusions and CUDA coverage limits. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Changed-file checks passed, no unrelated refactor or new steady-state synchronization. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Problem, dependency stack, evidence and limitations documented.

+            # Captured shapes must keep the even split the graph was captured
+            # with, and decode-sized steps are already realistic.
+            assert split is None

+        assert min(split) > 0
+        # Every request is either a real decode query or a prefill chunk. The
+        # even split this replaces gave all 128 requests num_tokens / 128
+        # queries, so there would be no decode requests left at all.
